tasks.short: Discuss grades with supervisors and complete grade paperwork

steps.what: Prepare grade-related paperwork and supporting marked-work references for supervisors
Meet with supervisors to discuss students' grades and resolve marking questions
Complete required grade-related paperwork according to the supervisor's decisions

tasks.design: Populate the supervisor pack from checked {LMS} records into a native {DOCS} template. Keep the discussion and recording of resulting decisions human, including any final entry into the {OTHER} assessment administration system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Grade meetings require repeated copying of marks and locating the same evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exports and linked templates can assemble the pack without interpreting performance.
tasks.still_hard: Disagreements, missing evidence and defensible grade decisions need supervisor discussion.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant explains the student's reasoning and the basis for marking choices.
tasks.altitude: Bring traceable evidence to grade discussions with less copying.

reach.task: Resolve disputed marks and specify the required records
reach.learn: Evidence needed for a defensible academic decision

evidence.claim: Native exports and document fields can reduce repeated grade-pack assembly; this is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Boundary begins with already marked work and ends with supervisor paperwork; original marking, recording the original grade list and official result release are excluded.

Existing markers produce the grade register and marked work in the normal assessment process. In s1 the assistant checks and captures student and assessment IDs, mark version, rubric reference, evidence links and the discussion issue; all checking, missing-evidence retrieval and capture are included in its 14 remaining hours.
Supervisor decisions are produced in s2 and entered manually in s3; no structured decision code or automated grade amendment is assumed.
Test native exports and templates first. Unmatched records are assembled manually, and pre-existing pack generation earns no saving.
unknowns: Supervisor form requirements and access controls
research_questions: Can an exported pack preserve correct grade versions and linked marking evidence without extra reconciliation?

already_counted.description: Pack checking, capture and evidence exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=14+45+20=79; gross 21%, less 3 upkeep gives net 18%. Low 0 if packs already exist or evidence reconciliation consumes the saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Schedule and maintain office hours for students

steps.what: Schedule regular office hours, publish availability and reconcile calendar changes
Maintain office hours to meet students and respond to their questions

tasks.design: Use a recurring schedule in {CALENDAR}, linked from {LMS}, to reduce repeated availability messages. The assistant checks and approves each published schedule version and keeps all student consultation time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Office-hour details and timetable changes are repeatedly typed into messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recurring events and a single availability link reduce re-entry without selecting students or replacing meetings.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting commitments and students unable to use standard hours need accommodation.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant provides attentive help and finds alternatives for students who need them.
tasks.altitude: Maintain a dependable published schedule while preserving time available to students.

reach.task: Coordinate room and timetable changes affecting office hours

evidence.claim: Native recurring calendars and an availability link can reduce repeated scheduling messages; the time estimate is E1.

assumptions: Boundary includes scheduling and holding office hours, not separate grading or tutoring sessions. The large live consultation share remains unchanged.

In s1 the assistant produces and checks dates, times, time zone, location or meeting link, exceptions and student access instructions from the timetable; its nine remaining hours include all capture, conflicts and approval.
a1 is given after the final schedule is assembled and before publication. Changes to dates, location or access instructions void it and require another check within s1.
Use native calendar recurrence first. No automatic booking, student prioritization or new student data capture is required; students retain their existing means of asking for an alternative.
unknowns: Existing calendar publishing and access arrangements
research_questions: Does a single checked recurring schedule reduce messages without reducing student access?

already_counted.description: Schedule capture, exception handling and approval

incremental.description: Check recurring schedule and link access

approvals.approved_version: Exact recurring schedule version with dates, exceptions, time zone, location and access instructions; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=9+85=94; gross 6%, less 1 upkeep gives net 5%. Low 0 if recurring scheduling already exists or exceptions use the small saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Confirm materials needed for classes and check existing stock or access
Prepare material requests using existing catalogue and course details
Order authorized materials or collect them and confirm suitability for class

tasks.design: Use saved request fields and catalogue items in {PROCUREMENT} after the assistant checks the class need and existing supplies. The assistant retains authorization coordination, order commitment, collection and suitability checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests repeatedly copy course references, material identifiers and delivery details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue requests can prefill established facts while quantities and substitutions remain checked.
tasks.still_hard: Specific teaching needs, access rights and shortages often require a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant knows whether the material is actually suitable for the class.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated requisition entry without changing purchasing rights.

reach.task: Confirm approved material sources and order authorization
reach.learn: Catalogue identifiers, licensing and delivery constraints

evidence.claim: Saved catalogue requests can reduce repeated entry; this task-specific scenario is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is confirming class materials, requesting and obtaining them; central procurement and supplier fulfilment are unchanged and earn no focal-role saving.
The assistant produces item identity, specification or edition, quantity, required date, stock checked and class reference in s1, retaining 35 hours including physical stock checks and capture.

In s2 the assistant checks catalogue match, unit, delivery address and cost reference within 15 remaining hours. Existing purchasing staff maintain catalogue fields in their normal process; no new supplier integration or free catalogue cleanup is assumed.
Test native saved requests first. Missing catalogue items are entered manually and substitutions require human discussion in s3; no automatic external order is introduced.
unknowns: Catalogue coverage and current saved-request use
research_questions: How much repeated request entry remains after catalogue and quantity checking?

incremental.description: Maintain saved request fields and catalogue references

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+15+35=85; gross 15%, less 3 upkeep gives net 12%. Low 0 for existing saved requests or frequent unmatched materials. Physical collection stays fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify classroom material version, recipients and digital or paper access requirements
Copy classroom materials and prepare the required distribution packs
Distribute classroom materials and resolve access or paper-copy problems

tasks.design: Use one verified file in {LMS} for classes where digital distribution is already permitted, reducing unnecessary copying and pack collation from {DOCS}. The assistant checks the package before release and retains all distribution, required paper handling and access support.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper packs are copied and collated even when recipients can use an approved digital version.
tasks.enabler_now: Native course-file sharing can replace avoidable duplication without a new content-generation tool.
tasks.still_hard: Some students and classroom activities require paper, accessible formats or help reaching the file.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant makes sure each student actually receives a usable version.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time making avoidable copies while retaining equitable access.

reach.task: Confirm which classroom resources may be distributed digitally
reach.learn: Course access needs, copyright and format restrictions

evidence.claim: Native digital file sharing can replace avoidable copying where teaching and access needs permit; this is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is copying and distribution of already approved materials, not authoring. No learning activity is assumed to accept a new format without instructor confirmation.
In s1 the assistant produces file/version, class ID, recipient scope, access requirements, copyright restrictions and required paper quantity; all verification and capture retain 30 hours.

The central scenario assumes most copying is avoidable because digital access is already permitted. s2's seven remaining hours include uploading or linking, preview checks and unavoidable paper preparation. If paper is required widely, the saving does not apply.

s3 retains all 35 hours for final package and recipient verification, explicit release approval, physical delivery and access exceptions. a1 follows the package creation in s2 and binds its exact version and audience; changes require reapproval.
Test native course sharing first. Already digital distribution earns no new saving. Only active copying and collation labour is counted, never printer runtime.
unknowns: Proportion of paper copies genuinely avoidable
Existing digital sharing and student access requirements
research_questions: Can approved digital delivery remove active copy preparation without increasing access support or required paper work?

already_counted.description: Digital package preparation and required copying
Release approval, distribution and access support

incremental.description: Maintain links, permissions and format guidance

approvals.approved_version: Exact prepared file package version, recipient class, access settings and paper-copy allocation; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+7+35=72; gross 28%, less 3 upkeep gives net 25%. Low 0 when paper is required or sharing already replaces copying. All actual distribution effort is retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated paperwork and avoidable copies while preserving student consultations and academic decisions.
reach: Confirm resource access with course instructors
role.ambitious_version: An assistant who keeps course administration dependable and spends protected time helping students.
